title: Night crossing
scenario: The night ferry runs a different set of routes between the quay and the lighthouse. Starting at the quay, can you reach the lighthouse?

intro.job: The night ferry runs a different set of routes between the quay and the lighthouse. Starting at the quay, can you reach the lighthouse?

idea.rule: The seen set is the memory — without it, the walk goes in circles forever.
idea.detail: Same question as Ferry routes, new map. Walk from the start: if you're at the target, yes; otherwise try each route out and ask the same question from there. Here almost every route has a partner running back the other way — the marina leads back to the quay — so a walk with no memory turns straight round. Keep a set of the stops you've been to, and never walk into one again.

model_restatement: Say whether the lighthouse can be reached from the quay.

clarify.question: Can a route lead back to a stop I just left?
clarify.answer: Yes — the marina's first route goes straight back to the quay. Your walk has to survive that.

clarify.question: What if there's no way to reach the target?
What about a dead end with no routes out?
clarify.answer: Then that way fails — try the next route.

clarify.question: Do I need the shortest way, or just whether I can get there?
clarify.answer: Just whether you can get there: True or False.

clarify_fallback: Good question — assume the simple case.
blueprint: To reach the target from a stop: if this stop is the target, yes. Otherwise try each route out of it, and ask the same question from where it leads. If none works, no.

checkpoints.prompt: The first call reaches line 2. Which stop is node?
The walk takes its first route. On the next call, which stop is node?
With the fix — after the second stop is remembered, what is seen?

why_line: The draft walks quay → marina → quay → marina… — the marina's first route leads back to the quay, so the walk never gets to the channel. A walk with no memory follows the loop forever.

explain.rule: A walk with no memory is a ferry that forgets where it came from — at the marina, the route back to the quay looks as new as any other.
explain.bridge: The walk goes quay → marina → quay. What would it need to know at the marina to take the channel route instead?

fix.rule: Carry a seen set: add each stop as you leave it, and never walk into a stop that's already in it.

walk.gloss: The first call starts an empty memory...
Remember this stop before walking on.
Only walk to stops not already seen.

contrast.wrong: for nxt in graph[node]: if can_reach(...)
contrast.right: if nxt not in seen and can_reach(..., seen)

alternatives.note: The same walk with an explicit to-do stack: a stop is marked seen when it's taken off the stack, and stops already seen are skipped.

hints: Follow the draft from the quay. Where does the marina's first route lead?
Nothing stops the walk from going straight back to a stop it just left.
Pass a seen set along: seen.add(node), and only walk to nxt if nxt not in seen.

follow_up.prompt: Same map — start at the marina, target the beacon. What does your code print?

checkpoint.prompt: With the marina as the start and the beacon as the target, what gets printed?

follow_up.fix_hint: The seen set lets it walk past the loop — marina → channel → beacon.

one_liner: The seen set is the memory — without it, the walk goes in circles forever.
